status_note: diagnostic of the row I3 FAIL under amendment I3-FU-1; no gate; row I3 is not re-graded
redistribution_note: This file contains aggregate statistics only; no libdEdx/ICRU 73 table values, per-energy deviations or ratios are reproduced.
rounding_note: every table-relative band mean (ions, informative_z1_z2, i3b default) is rounded to 0.1 percentage point (round(d, 3) in relative units) before it is written and before any derived quantity is computed; z-scan fits, shape_ratio_to_z6, prediction_from_z3_10_fit, hypothesis_check and the z-scan verdicts use the rounded means only, so nothing here depends on an unrounded mean. 0.1 pp is the precision already present in Git (plan results note of 2026-11-15). Reason: the [10, 20) band holds two grid points and row I3 publishes the >= 10 MeV/u maximum (at 10 MeV/u for a monotone deficit), so a full-precision mean would give the deviation at the other point; at 0.1 pp it is fixed only to +-0.1 pp. The quantisation limits the z-scan in the [20, 50) band (deviations of a few 0.1 pp). The C/O band maxima (2-10, >= 10 MeV/u) are at full precision: row I3 already publishes them
i_value_note: The ionmc model is evaluated at I = 78 eV (water(78.0), not tuned). libdEdx lists I = 75.0 eV for target 276 (dedx_metadata.h material constant). Whether the ICRU73_NEW water values were computed with 75 eV or 78 eV: TO-VERIFY (P5b); the archive documentation (README.md, data/README.md, tools/dat2c.py, the dedx_icru73new.h header) states no I-value for this table. If 75 eV, the known bounded contribution of the difference is about 0.4-0.6 % in S above 10 MeV/u and 0.4-0.5 % in CSDA range (plan row I3, L0 ~ -ln I; model S lower and range longer at 78 eV); a range-clause failure within that bound is recorded as FAIL with this attribution, never re-graded.

hypothesis_check.rule: amendment I3-FU-1 rule 1a: CONFIRMED iff, for carbon12 and oxygen16, every band mean of [2,5), [5,10), [10,20), [20,50) MeV/u rounded to 0.1 pp equals the quoted value (|delta| <= 0.05 pp before rounding) and |rounded mean of [50,1000]| <= the quoted bound (0.03 % C, 0.06 % O); otherwise WITHDRAWN. The bounds are below the 0.1 pp quantum, so the last condition means a rounded mean of 0 (|mean| < 0.05 pp). The quoted >= 50 MeV/u figure was a max-type statement; a mean checks it only partly

z_scan.method: per band, least squares d_z = c f(z) without intercept over Z = 3-10; d_z the band mean of S_model/S_table - 1 rounded to 0.1 pp; charge: f = band mean of 1 - q^2/z^2 (model effective charge); barkas_like: f = z; bloch_like: f = z^2; constant: f = 1 (z-independent control); r_squared uncentred (1 - sum res^2 / sum d^2); ranking by residual RMS
z_scan.verdict_rule: amendment I3-FU-1 rule 1b: with RMS_1 <= RMS_2 the two smallest residual RMS and r^2_1 that of the best shape, attributed_to = best iff RMS_1 <= 0.5 RMS_2, r^2_1 >= 0.90 and the rounded d_z over Z = 3-10 have one common sign (no zero, no sign change); otherwise attributed_to = null (no single-term scaling explains the z-dependence in this band) with reason in {rms_ratio, r_squared, sign_change}. Interpretive, not a grade

informative_z1_z2.lineage_note: table lineage for Z = 1, 2 OPEN: excluded from the z-scan fits (Z = 3-10); band means and the predictions of the Z = 3-10 fits are informative only

i3b.note: informative; table-relative band means for the default variant only (duplicate of the rounded ions entry); all variants carry model-only quantities (CSDA-range shift vs the default model from BetheStoppingSource tables, 1-500 MeV/u, 200 points/decade; band-mean stopping ratio r_v to the default model). Variant-vs-table band means are not written: eight of them at full precision would let the per-energy table values of a band with <= 8 grid points be solved for; the variant-vs-table mean is approximately (1 + d_default) r_v - 1

provenance.mass_note: Li-7, Be-9, B-11, N-14, F-19 and Ne-20 use the nuclear mass A u - Z m_e (mass number times the atomic mass unit minus Z electron masses; mass excess and electron binding neglected). Model-only sensitivity: a 0.1 % mass increase changes the nitrogen14 stopping by at most 0.000799 (relative) over the grid at E >= 2 MeV/u.
